meta.input: A daily habit tracker app for busy professionals
meta.note: Every metric below is a placeholder. Replace [bracketed] values with real measurements before publishing anything. The viral-engine honesty guardrails forbid invented social proof.
meta.disclaimer: This is a worked example of the skill's output format, not a case study with verified results.

bet.what: A daily habit tracker pitch repositioned from wellness utility to career-risk management.
bet.who: Second- and third-year university students in competitive placement tracks who have already downloaded and abandoned two habit apps.
bet.why_it_spreads: The share isn't 'here's a habit app' (boring, everyone has one). It's 'here's the thing that stops you from blowing your placement' — which is a reputation-safe share because it makes the sender look disciplined and generous at the same time.
bet.biggest_risk: Students are saturated with productivity content and can smell a guru instantly. The frame dies if it sounds like a hustle-culture course.

diagnosis.bottleneck_as_given: surprise + identity (tied at 1). 'Habit tracker for busy professionals' is a category with zero tension and no tribe.
diagnosis.bottleneck_after: emotion (3). The career-risk frame is clear and shareable but only mildly activating — it needs one concrete story to spike.
diagnosis.verdict: Do not run a launch on the original framing. Reposition first, then test hooks. The product does not need to change; the category does.

hooks.text: The app my professor doesn't want you to use (but your GPA depends on it).
hooks.target: Students who already suspect the system is stacked against them
hooks.why_it_works: Names an authority conflict in eleven words. The parenthetical resolves the curiosity gap just enough to make clicking feel safe, not risky.
hooks.risk: Slightly adversarial toward professors. Keep the tone playful, never actually anti-education, or faculty will push back.

hooks.text: I tracked 4 habits for 30 days. My placement offer came on day 26.
hooks.why_it_works: A dateable, arguable claim with a real number. Invites 'wait, which habits?' replies, which are free distribution.
hooks.risk: Only usable if the story is true. If it is, this is the strongest hook in the set — it converts a utility into a narrative.

hooks.text: 47 browser tabs, 3 deadlines, 0 systems. This is for you.
hooks.target: Students in exam crunch who self-identify as chaotic
hooks.why_it_works: Hyper-specific scene-setting. The reader recognizes themselves in one second, which is the whole job of line one.
hooks.risk: Peeks as mildly insulting. Soften with humor in line two.

positioning.crowded_category: Habit tracker / productivity app — thousands of competitors, zero urgency, no reason to switch.
positioning.sentence: It's not a habit tracker. It's placement-risk management — for students who are one missed deadline away from a bad semester.

rejected_frames.why_rejected: True and important, but it invites clinical claims the app can't back, and it makes sharing feel heavy rather than useful.
Requires a network effect on day one. Cold-start problem kills it before the hook has a chance.

positioning.proof_required: The frame only survives if the app visibly ties a habit to an outcome the student cares about (submission dates, interview prep, sleep before an exam). Otherwise 'placement-risk management' is a costume.

share_mechanisms.implementation: A shareable 'Semester Risk Score' card: three numbers (habits held, deadlines hit, sleep hours) rendered as a screenshot-friendly graphic with no personal data.
share_mechanisms.cost_to_sharer: One tap, zero explanation needed because the card is self-describing.
share_mechanisms.why_chosen: Students already screenshot their stats for group chats. Give them a better-looking artifact and they will do it for you.

share_mechanisms.implementation: On the streak screen, one button: 'Send my risk card to the friend who needs it.' Pre-written message, editable, no referral spam.
share_mechanisms.cost_to_sharer: Low — framed as a favor, not a promo.
share_mechanisms.why_chosen: Turns the existing peer dynamic (students nagging each other about deadlines) into a distribution channel.

structure.rejected_mechanisms: Leaderboards were cut. They convert well for the top 5% and shame everyone else, which suppresses sharing among exactly the people who need the app.

content_skeleton.line_2_3: Most habit apps are built for people who already have their life together. This one is built for the week before submissions.
middle_proofs: Real number: [X] students used it through one exam cycle.
Story: the day-26 placement offer, told in 4 sentences with dates.
Mechanism: a visible risk score instead of a vague streak, so progress is legible in a screenshot.
content_skeleton.turn: The point isn't discipline. It's having one number that tells you whether this week is on fire before it actually is.
content_skeleton.close: Try it for one semester. If your risk score doesn't drop in two weeks, delete it.

seed_nodes: Placement-prep Telegram groups at 3 named universities (join, contribute for a week, then share)
r/college and r/GetStudying — read the self-promo rules first; post as a build log, not an ad
Two student-run Instagram pages in the target city with real engagement
The professor or TA who runs the placement cell — a single endorsement outperforms 20 posts
One Discord for CS interview prep where the maintainers are active
distribution.first_100: Hand-recruit 20 students for a 2-week beta. Requirement: they must send you their risk card once. Their cards are the first 20 pieces of social proof and the first 20 share events. No public launch until 10 of them say they'd be annoyed if you shut it down.
distribution.share_sentence: This is the thing that tells you your semester is on fire before it actually is — made for students, not CEOs.
distribution.loop: Risk card → sent to a friend → friend installs to compare → their card is now a new send → repeat. The loop is peer comparison, not referrals.
distribution.backstop: Exam-season search intent ('submission deadline tracker') plus a free printable semester planner that ranks on its own. If the spike never comes, this keeps the lights on.

first_48_hours: Hour 0-2: Replace the README/store copy with the new category. Same product, new frame. No feature work.
Hour 2-4: Build the risk card as a static image from real data. Ship the ugly version today.
Hour 4-6: Write the day-26 story in 4 sentences. If it isn't true, write the true version instead — do not invent one.
Day 1 evening: DM 20 students individually. Ask for one card, not a testimonial.
Day 2 morning: Post the build log to one community whose rules allow it. Answer every comment yourself.
Day 2 evening: Read the first 20 replies manually. If the frame is landing, do nothing else. If it isn't, change the hook only — not the product.

hook_rate.action_if_low: Rewrite line one; keep everything else identical.

share_ratio.action_if_low: The send button is either invisible or the card isn't worth sending. Test the artifact before the copy.

retention.metric: 7-day return rate after first risk card
retention.action_if_low: You have a spike, not a product. Stop all promotion and fix the core loop.

failure_condition: This fails if students read 'placement-risk management' as another adult telling them to be more disciplined. Test the frame with 5 students verbally before publishing it anywhere.

guardrail_check.single_call_to_action: Yes — try it for one semester.
guardrail_check.platform_rules_checked: Flagged for the subreddit self-promo rule.
